title: 132 New York Artists Receive $903,000 in Grants
summary: The NYSCA/NYFA Artist Fellowship program awards each recipient $8,000 in unrestricted cash.

title: Former V&A Academic Programs Head Accuses Museum of “Racist” Behavior
summary: A recently shared letter from Yuko Kikuchi, who resigned from her post in January, asks the British institution to address its “culture of systemic racism.”

title: Meet the Curators of the Next “Made in LA”
summary: Michael Wellen and José Luis Blondet get the nod, Tate names a new director, and the Immigrant Artist Biennial is back for another edition.

title: Mayor Mamdani Should Reclaim the City’s Jefferson Statue
summary: The fact that the quill of David d’Angers’s statue of the third US president broke during the nation’s 250th anniversary provides more than an irresistible symbolic trope.

title: Giant Wieners, Drag Queens, and Curtis Sliwa at “The Most American Pageant Ever!”
summary: The absurdist performance art event at Times Square felt more like an elegy during this national moment.

title: Required Reading
summary: This week: the Louvre reopens the room where it happens, a Texas artist’s outdoor collection, Nancy Drew in the public domain, Rachel Cusk and Natalie Portman have beef, and more.

title: David Hockney’s Endless Scroll
summary: The late artist’s digital paintings at Serpentine, Tate gets a new director, beyond the myth of Brazilian modernist Chico da Silva, and more.

title: Protesters Decry Chinatown Museum’s Acceptance of “Jail Money” at Town Hall
summary: Leaders of New York’s Museum of Chinese failed to persuade protesters that a $35 million grant from the city was not tied to the construction of a borough jail.

title: Tate Names Dia Leader Jessica Morgan as Next Director
summary: The British curator will return to London to helm the museum network beginning next year.

title: Beyond the Myth of Chico da Silva
summary: Presenting da Silva with Amazonian artists of different generations undermines the Western notion of the artist as an isolated genius.

title: Remembering Christine Borland, John Will, and Astrid Furnival
summary: This week, we honor an artist who explored human fragility through science, a pioneering British textile artist, and a champion of digital art.

title: You Can Love David Hockney and Still Hate His iPad Paintings
summary: No amount of curatorial artspeak counters the sense that the late artist’s massive digital painting lacks the inventive mark-making and use of color that characterized his life’s work.

title: Artists Sue NYC Gallery The Hole for Nonpayment
summary: The suit filed by Daniel Um and Nastaran Shahbazi concerns nearly $50,000 in payments allegedly owed to the artists.

title: Juliana Huxtable and Mark Bradford in Major Gift to the Zimmerli Art Museum
summary: Collectors Anne and Arthur Goldstein have gifted over 70 works of modern and contemporary art to the Rutgers University museum.

title: Jimothy, Meme and Muse
summary: Artists share tributes to the beloved raccoon, plus Sabri Sundos’s odes to Palestinian diaspora and memory.
